note: Sources whose records are public. A person with at least one citation from one of these is not treated as living (David, 16 October 2026: 'any sources such as those publicly available are automatically deemed ok to show, e.g. FamilySearch, MyHeritage, Findmypast'). A match is a case-insensitive substring of the citation's provider, URL or title. This lists RECORD collections only: a private family-tree entry (a MyHeritage, Ancestry or Geni TREE profile, a GEDCOM, family lore) is not on it and does not count. Edit this file to change the rule for every archive; each archive reads it through kit/tools/living_rule.py. FamilySearch always counts, including its Family Tree, because FamilySearch hides living people (David, 16 October 2026). MyHeritage files other sites' user-built trees (Geni's World Family Tree, WikiTree, Filae, GenealogieOnline) under 'research' or 'Collection'; those are private-tree entries, not records, so they are excluded (found 16 Oct 2026 by the Blazevic agent: 20 living people would otherwise have counted as public-sourced and been shown with dates).
